turns.script: How do I undo my last commit?
turns.asr_text: How do I undo my last commit?

turns.text_generated: Hey, great question! If you want to undo your last commit, it depends on whether you’ve pushed it to a remote repository or not. If you haven’t pushed it yet, you can use the command `git reset HEAD~1` to remove the commit but keep your changes. If you want to completely discard the changes, you can add the `--hard` flag: `git reset --hard HEAD~1`. If you’ve already pushed the commit, you might want to use `git revert HEAD` instead, because that creates a new commit that undoes the changes, which is safer for shared branches. That way, your repository stays tidy and coordinated.
